definitions.type: extended diameter of a subset of an emetric space
definitions.definition: For an emetric space W and B⊆W, ediam(B)=sup{edist(x,y):x,y∈B} in ℝ≥0∞; the empty supremum is zero.

definitions.type: real diameter of a bounded subset of a metric space
definitions.definition: For a bounded subset B of a metric space W, diam(B)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y∈B}, with diam(∅)=0. Its cast to ℝ≥0∞ is ediam(B). This notation is used only after boundedness has been established.

For an emetric space W, B⊆W, real a and r∈ℝ≥0∞, content(a,r,B)= inf_{U:ℕ→Set W} inf_{B⊆⋃i U_i} inf_{∀i ediam(U_i)≤r} Σ'_i sup_{h:U_i nonempty} ediam(U_i)^a. Infima and sums take values in ℝ≥0∞. A failed condition has empty infimum ∞; the supremum over a nonemptiness proof is zero for an empty member. This is exactly BasisObjects.content in basis-registry.json /lean_header.

For a metric space W, B⊆W, a>0 and δ>0, C^a_δ(B)=content(a,ENNReal.ofReal δ,B). The original real-diameter convention is the infimum of Σ_i diam(U_i)^a over countable covers of B with diam(U_i)≤δ, empty members contributing zero. The proof establishes compatibility of these two formulations.

output.statement: For every metric space X, subset A⊆X and real a>0, the positive-scale contents C^a_δ(A) are exactly the unnormalized real-diameter countable-cover contents of the original problem. Finite or countable index families can be reindexed into ℕ with empty padding and unchanged cost. For 0<δ₁≤δ₂, C^a_δ₂(A)≤C^a_δ₁(A). Each admissible δ-cover has cost at least C^a_δ(A), and every lower bound for all admissible costs bounds C^a_δ(A) below (including when no cover exists). H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0} C^a_δ(A), so C^a_δ(A)≤H^a(A). For δ>0, C^a_δ(A)=0 iff for every real ε>0 there is an admissible countable δ-cover with a-cost <ε. Consequently H^a(A)=0 iff such covers exist at every positive δ and every positive ε. All costs and infima are in ℝ≥0∞; empty members contribute zero.

locals.declaration: Fix any metric space X and equip it with its Borel measurable structure.
Fix real a; temporarily assume L1: a>0.
Fix an arbitrary real scale δ; positive-scale uses are under the stated local antecedents.
Fix an arbitrary real tolerance ε; positivity is the local antecedent in S002.
In the extended-scale comparison let r range over positive extended scales; its finite and infinite cases are treated explicitly.
For the scale-monotonicity proof fix any real δ₁.
For the scale-monotonicity proof fix any real δ₂.

argument.text: Fix X,A,a and assume L1: a>0. Work with X's Borel structure, so M001 applies and gives H^a(A)=sup_{r>0} content(a,r,A) over extended nonnegative r. For arbitrary δ, temporarily assume L2: δ>0. At the finite scale ofReal δ, every admissible covering member has finite extended diameter, hence is bounded and has ediam equal to its real diameter cast to ℝ≥0∞. The nonemptiness-proof supremum in D004 is the displayed diameter power on a nonempty member and is zero on an empty member. For a>0 this agrees with assigning the empty member diameter zero and 0^a=0. Thus the nested infima are exactly the original admissible-cover infimum, with no prefactor. A finite family can be padded by empty sets. For an arbitrary countable index type choose an injection into ℕ; at each image index put the unique original member and elsewhere put ∅. This preserves the union and all nonnegative sums. Conversely an ℕ-family is countable. Discharge L2 after this finite-scale interpretation, retaining its δ>0 antecedent for every δ. For arbitrary δ₁,δ₂, temporarily assume L3: 0<δ₁≤δ₂. Every δ₁-cover is a δ₂-cover, so C^a_δ₂(A)≤C^a_δ₁(A). Discharge L3 and quantify the two scales. Every cost bounds its infimum above; a lower bound on every admissible cost bounds the infimum below. If the admissible family is empty its infimum is ∞, and the latter assertion remains true. For any positive extended scale r, if it is finite it is the cast of a positive real scale. The content at r=∞ is at most that at any fixed finite positive scale, since every finite-scale cover is also an ∞-cover. Hence the ∞ scale adds nothing to the supremum. We have proved H^a(A)=sup_{δ>0}C^a_δ(A), and each such content is ≤H^a(A).

produces.statement: Under a>0, the contents have the real-diameter countable-cover interpretation with empty padding/reindexing; they are nonincreasing in positive scale, satisfy the two infimum bounds, and H^a(A)=sup_{δ_bound>0}C^a_{δ_bound}(A).

argument.text: For the arbitrary δ,ε, temporarily assume L4: δ>0 and ε>0. Suppose L5: C^a_δ(A)=0. if every admissible cost were ≥ε, the lower-bound property in F001 would imply C^a_δ(A)≥ε>0, a contradiction. Thus an admissible cover of cost <ε exists. Discharge L5 to obtain the forward implication. In terms of the nested infima in D004, any failed cover or diameter condition has value ∞ and cannot give a value <ε, so the approximation provides an actual admissible family. Conversely assume L6: for every positive tolerance there exists an admissible cover of smaller cost. This forces the nonnegative content to be zero: a positive value, finite or infinite, has some positive finite real below it, contradicting the upper bound by those costs. Discharge L6, then L4, and quantify the arbitrary positive scale and tolerance. This proves the zero-content approximation equivalence for every positive scale. These arguments also cover an empty admissible family, whose content is ∞.

produces.statement: For every δ_bound>0, C^a_{δ_bound}(A)=0 iff at every positive finite real tolerance there exists an admissible countable δ_bound-cover of A of smaller a-cost.

argument.text: By F001, H^a(A)=0 implies each positive-scale content is zero; F002 then gives the required arbitrarily small covers at every scale. Conversely, those covers make every positive-scale content zero by F002, and their supremum is zero by F001. This proves the full equivalence and all asserted content properties. Discharge L1 to retain a>0 as an antecedent and universally quantify X,A,a and the scale/tolerance variables. No boundedness or measurability assumption on A is used.

applications.bindings: Take W=X with its Borel structure, exponent a and set A; expand the extended-scale content exactly as D004.
